t: The Crown Estate isn't a single building. It's a collection of lands and holdings across the United Kingdom that belong to the British monarch as a corporation sole. That makes it the sovereign's public estate, which is neither government property nor the monarch's private property. In England, Wales and Northern Ireland the Crown Estate Commissioners manage it. Scotland's share has been run separately by Crown Estate Scotland since 2017. George the Third, who reigned from 1760 to 1820, is named as its founder, and he was the first Hanoverian monarch born in Great Britain.
